perspective:
**Keith Ndiaye’s available information:**

- Keith is a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist there. They are colleagues with a friendly but professional relationship, usually interacting during Keith’s office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith noticed Elizabeth was unusually curt/short with him. He thought she might be upset with him, possibly because of an unknown misunderstanding or mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe. He suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her or overstepped, and he felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth said he didn’t overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed that Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he’s always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts or any details of her stress beyond what she explicitly told him or what he observed.
